ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The transition-state structure in the attached figure contains a left-side R4-connected carbon center, multiple oxygen atoms, a right-side carbon center bearing R2 and R3, and a lower C=N fragment; the figure also draws O-H and N-H^+ related labels and curved arrows. Reasoning: Scanning from left to right and counting only the bonds drawn between non-hydrogen atoms, there are 9 single bonds in total: R4-C, upper-left C-O, C-O bridge bond, C-O lower bond, lower O-C, bridge O-C(R2/R3), C-R2, C-R3, and N-R1. The C=N double bond is counted as 2 bonds. Excluding the bonds involving hydrogen in O-H and N-H, and ignoring the arrows. Therefore the total is 9 + 2 = 11.

raw_record.question_text:
In the transition-state structure shown in the image, calculate the total number of bonds in the structure, including single, double, and triple bonds but excluding those involving hydrogen.

Note: Disregard arrows. Consider all components present in the transition-state structure.

method.method_draft: Scan the image from left to right and mark each non-hydrogen bond drawn as a line. Count the nine single bonds between non-H atoms/residue labels: R4-C, C-O(top-left), C-O(bridge), C-O(bottom), O(bottom)-C, O(bridge)-C(R2/R3), C-R2, C-R3, and N-R1. Then count the C=N double bond as two bonds. Exclude O-H and N-H even though they are drawn/indicated, and ignore all arrows. Total = 9 + 2 = 11.

method.method_draft: Partition the visible non-H skeleton.
